\chapter{Chapter06 — ANF}

\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter06.F₂Polynomials.ANF}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Binary-valued function on the cube]
\lean{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.𝔽₂}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p019-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p020-b001
}
For a natural number $n$, a binary-valued function on the $n$-dimensional cube is a
function from $\mathbb F_2^n$ to $\mathbb F_2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Support of a binary function]
\lean{FABL.f₂OneSupport}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p018-b003}
For a function $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2$, its one-support is the set of points
$x\in\mathbb F_2^n$ such that $f(x)=1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Hamming norm and support size]
\lean{FABL.hammingNorm_eq_card_f₂OneSupport}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.f₂OneSupport}
\difficulty{4}
For every function $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2$, its Hamming norm equals the number
of inputs $x\in\mathbb F_2^n$ for which $f(x)=1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[ANF coefficient assignments]
\lean{FABL.ANFCoefficients}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p149-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p169-b008
}
\label{FABL.ANFCoefficients}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.𝔽₂}
For a natural number $n$, an assignment of algebraic normal form coefficients is a
function from the subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ to $\mathbb F_2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Algebraic normal form monomial]
\lean{FABL.anfMonomial}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p149-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p169-b008
}
\label{FABL.anfMonomial}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.𝔽₂}
For a subset $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and a point $x\in\mathbb F_2^n$, define the
associated monomial by $\prod_{i\in S}x_i$, with the empty product equal to $1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Evaluation of an algebraic normal form]
\lean{FABL.anfEval}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p149-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p169-b008
}
\label{FABL.anfEval}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ANFCoefficients, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.anfMonomial, FABL.𝔽₂}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $c$ assign a coefficient in $\mathbb{F}_2$ to each subset of
$\Fin(n)$, and let $x \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$. The evaluation of the algebraic normal form with
coefficients $c$ at $x$ is the sum, over all subsets $S$ of $\Fin(n)$, of $c(S)$ times the
monomial indexed by $S$ evaluated at $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Support of an algebraic normal form]
\lean{FABL.anfSupport}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p169-b008}
\label{FABL.anfSupport}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ANFCoefficients}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $c$ assign a coefficient in $\mathbb{F}_2$ to each subset of
$\Fin(n)$. The support of $c$ is the set of all subsets $S \subseteq \Fin(n)$ for which $c(S)
\ne 0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Algebraic degree of coefficients]
\lean{FABL.algebraicDegree}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b007,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p036-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p149-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p169-b008
}
\label{FABL.algebraicDegree}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ANFCoefficients, FABL.anfSupport}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $c$ assign a coefficient in $\mathbb{F}_2$ to each subset of
$\Fin(n)$. Its algebraic degree is the largest cardinality of a subset in its support, with
degree $0$ when the support is empty.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Characterization of ANF support]
\lean{FABL.mem_anfSupport}
\label{FABL.mem_anfSupport}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ANFCoefficients, FABL.anfSupport}
\difficulty{1}
Let $c$ assign an element of $\mathbb F_2$ to every subset of $[n]$. A subset
$S\subseteq[n]$ belongs to the support of $c$ if and only if its coefficient $c(S)$ is
nonzero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Empty monomial]
\lean{FABL.anfMonomial_empty}
\label{FABL.anfMonomial_empty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.anfMonomial}
\difficulty{1}
For any natural number $n$ and any point $x$ in the Boolean cube $(\bbr/2\bbr)^n$, the
monomial indexed by the empty set has value $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Zero polynomial evaluation]
\lean{FABL.anfEval_zero}
\label{FABL.anfEval_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.anfEval}
\difficulty{1}
For any dimension $n$ and any point $x$ in the Boolean cube $\bbr^n$ over $\bbr/2\bbr$, the
algebraic normal form whose coefficient at every subset of coordinates is zero evaluates
to zero at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Additivity of polynomial evaluation]
\lean{FABL.anfEval_add}
\label{FABL.anfEval_add}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ANFCoefficients, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.anfEval}
\difficulty{3}
Let $c$ and $d$ be coefficient families indexed by subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let
$x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. Evaluating the coefficientwise sum $c+d$ at $x$ gives the sum of
their evaluations:
$\operatorname{ANF}(c+d)(x)=\operatorname{ANF}(c)(x)+\operatorname{ANF}(d)(x)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Product of Boolean monomials]
\lean{FABL.anfMonomial_mul}
\label{FABL.anfMonomial_mul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.anfMonomial}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S$ and $T$ be finite sets of coordinates in $
{0,1}$, and let $x$ be a function from $
{0,1}$ to the field $\bbr/2\bbr$. The product of the monomials indexed by $S$ and $T$,
evaluated at $x$, equals the monomial indexed by $S\cup T$, evaluated at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Product of algebraic normal forms]
\lean{FABL.anfMul}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p169-b008}
\label{FABL.anfMul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ANFCoefficients}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $c$ and $d$ assign coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_2$ to subsets
of $\Fin(n)$. Their product has, at each subset $U \subseteq \Fin(n)$, coefficient equal to the
sum of $c(S)d(T)$ over all pairs of subsets $S,T \subseteq \Fin(n)$ whose union is $U$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of the product coefficients]
\lean{FABL.anfEval_anfMul}
\label{FABL.anfEval_anfMul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ANFCoefficients, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.anfEval, FABL.anfMonomial_mul, FABL.anfMul}
\difficulty{4}
Let $c$ and $d$ be coefficient families indexed by subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let
$x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. If the coefficient at $U$ of a new family is the sum of $c(S)d(T)$
over pairs of subsets with $S\cup T=U$, then its algebraic normal form evaluated at $x$
equals the product of the evaluations of $c$ and $d$ at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Algebraic degree bounded by dimension]
\lean{FABL.algebraicDegree_le_dimension}
\label{FABL.algebraicDegree_le_dimension}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ANFCoefficients, FABL.algebraicDegree}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, and let $c$ assign a coefficient in the field with two elements to
each subset of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Then $\deg(c)\le n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monomial on a subset indicator]
\lean{FABL.anfMonomial_f₂CubeOfFinset}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.anfMonomial, FABL.f₂CubeOfFinset, FABL.f₂CubeOfFinset_apply}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $S$ and $U$ be subsets of the coordinate set $\in
n$. Evaluating the monomial indexed by $S$ at the point that equals $1$ on $U$ and $0$
outside $U$ gives $1$ if $S\subseteq U$, and $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $c$ be a coefficient family indexed by subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and let
$U\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The algebraic normal form with coefficients $c$, evaluated
at the vector equal to $1$ on $U$ and $0$ elsewhere, is $\sum_{S\subseteq U}c(S)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Coefficients from function values]
\lean{FABL.anfCoeff}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p149-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p149-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p169-b008
}
\label{FABL.anfCoeff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ANFCoefficients, FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.f₂CubeOfFinset}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$. For each subset $S\subseteq\Fin(n)$,
its algebraic normal form coefficient is the sum of $f$ evaluated at the indicator
vectors of all subsets $T\subseteq S$.
\end{definition}

  {FABL.anfCoeff}
  {direct}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p164-b007}
\difficulty{6}
Let $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$ and let $U\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The algebraic
normal form whose coefficient at each set $S$ is the sum of $f(1_T)$ over all
$T\subseteq S$ evaluates at $1_U$ to $f(1_U)$, where $1_T$ denotes the vector equal to
$1$ on $T$ and $0$ elsewhere.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniqueness of algebraic normal form coefficients]
\lean{FABL.anfEval_injective}
\label{FABL.anfEval_injective}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ANFCoefficients, FABL.anfCoeff_unique_of_powerset_sum, FABL.anfEval, FABL.anfEval_f₂CubeOfFinset}
\difficulty{3}
Let $c$ and $d$ be coefficient families indexed by subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. If their
algebraic normal forms agree at every $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$, then $c=d$.
\end{theorem}
